mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES remains depressed, more trips are generated from home-based routines and nearby errands, which lifts retail and recreation visits within two weeks. The mechanism fails if a concurrent rise in transit and workplaces pulls activity away from local retail.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 4-week mean within 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 6 and WORKPLACES remaining below -10.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-on-week drop in TRANSIT by at least 3 points signals weaker central-area movement and lower discretionary shopping access, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next four weeks. The claim fails if retail rebounds while transit continues to weaken.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days even after TRANSIT declines by more than 3 points from one week to the next.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES drops sharply and stays below -20, it indicates a renewed restriction-like or remote-work regime that suppresses in-person shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within one week. The mechanism fails if retail rises despite the workplace pullback.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week after WORKPLACES crosses below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility is a warm-weather substitution signal: more outdoor leisure crowds coincide with more overall outing propensity, and retail-and-recreation follows higher over four weeks. This fails if park activity rises without any retail recovery.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days even though PARKS stays above its current 4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL also rises, households are consolidating non-discretionary trips near home, leaving less room for discretionary retail visits and pulling RETAIL_REC down over two weeks. The effect fails if grocery movement rises but retail improves anyway.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both remaining above their prior 4-week means.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES after a trough signals renewed daytime foot traffic that spills into nearby shopping and dining, which raises RETAIL_REC over the next month. The mechanism fails if workplace mobility improves but retail remains flat or lower.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES increases for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains below -40 and WORKPLACES also stays below -15, commuting frictions are suppressing discretionary trips to commercial districts, so RETAIL_REC declines within four weeks. The claim fails when retail recovers despite both mobility channels staying weak.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days while TRANSIT stays below -40 and WORKPLACES stays below -15.

mechanism_narrative: In a stable low-transit regime, a modest improvement in PARKS followed by higher RETAIL_REC reflects substitution from purely home-centered time toward broader outing bundles that include shopping and dining. The effect appears within one to two weeks and fails if park gains are not matched by retail gains.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days when PARKS rises while TRANSIT remains below -40.
